title: Implement Custom useMemo & useCallback Engine
problemStatement: Implement `createMemoEngine()` providing `useMemo(factory, deps)` and `useCallback(fn, deps)`. Only re-evaluates `factory` or returns a new function when `deps` change according to `Object.is`.
interviewTrap: `useCallback(fn, deps)` is literally just syntactic sugar for `useMemo(() => fn, deps)`.

testCases.name: useMemo caches computation when deps do not change
testCases.input: factory called once across multiple renders with same deps
testCases.testFn: const engine = createMemoEngine(); let calls = 0; const compute = () => { calls++; return 42; }; engine.useMemo(compute, [1]); engine.useMemo(compute, [1]); return calls;

testCases.name: useMemo recomputes when deps change
testCases.testFn: const engine = createMemoEngine(); let calls = 0; const compute = () => { calls++; return 100; }; engine.useMemo(compute, [1]); engine.useMemo(compute, [2]); return calls;

testCases.name: useCallback preserves function reference when deps match
testCases.testFn: const engine = createMemoEngine(); const cb1 = engine.useCallback(() => 1, ['id']); const cb2 = engine.useCallback(() => 1, ['id']); return cb1 === cb2;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Whenever a parent component re-renders, React re-renders every child component down the tree by default. `React.memo` stops this descent by checking if all props are identical using `Object.is`. Passing a new object or inline function reference `() => {}` forces re-rendering.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Hook-Level Memoization via Dependency Caching.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Hook-Level Memoization via Dependency Caching maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.
